evidence.quote: Problem 9.5.3 Can the algebraic hypersurface w 3 + wg(w1, ......, wn ) + f (w1 , ......, wn ) = 1, where g is homogeneous of degree 2 and f homogeneous of degree 3, be holomorphically immersed in Cn [ Not true for algebraic immersion] -R. Narasimhan, Dept. of Math., Univ. of Chicago, Chicago, IL 60637

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $n \geq 1$ and let $g, f \in \mathbb{C}[w_1, \ldots, w_n]$ be polynomials such that $g$ is homogeneous of degree $2$ and $f$ is homogeneous of degree $3$. Consider the algebraic hypersurface
$$X = \{(w, w_1, \ldots, w_n) \in \mathbb{C}^{n+1} : w^3 + w\, g(w_1, \ldots, w_n) + f(w_1, \ldots, w_n) = 1\}.$$
Here a holomorphic immersion of a complex manifold $M$ of dimension $n$ into $\mathbb{C}^n$ is a holomorphic map $\varphi : M \to \mathbb{C}^n$ whose differential is injective at every point of $M$ (no properness or injectivity of $\varphi$ is required).

Determine whether $X$ (viewed as a complex manifold, assumed smooth) admits a holomorphic immersion into $\mathbb{C}^n$. (It is known that no such immersion exists in the category of algebraic maps; the question is about the holomorphic category.)

status_evidence.title: Narasimhan embedding theorem (nLab)
status_evidence.snippet: Every Stein manifold of complex dimension n admits a proper holomorphic embedding into C^{2n+1} and a holomorphic immersion into C^{2n}.
status_evidence.claim: Standard immersion bounds for Stein manifolds; does not address the specific cubic hypersurface immersing into the optimal dimension C^n.
